extracted.intended_audience: prospective applicants to the John Templeton Foundation submitting an Online Funding Inquiry (OFI)
extracted.subtask_description: Instructions and standards for completing the John Templeton Foundation Online Funding Inquiry (OFI), describing required fields, format, eligibility, budget rules, and document/attachment guidance for applicants seeking project grants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project term maximum (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: A project has a specific start and end date. Generally, projects submitted to the Foundation may have a term of no more than 3 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should plan projects with defined start/end dates and normally not exceed 3 years total duration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cycle selection
rubrics_metrics.description: The Foundation accepts new funding inquiries (OFIs) at any time of the year. However, the Foundation reviews OFIs at specific times of the year depending upon the size of the request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review the Foundation’s grantmaking calendar and select the cycle that best aligns with your request; timing affects review and start dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding Area selection and triage
rubrics_metrics.description: Please select the Funding Area that best aligns with your proposed project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If unsure, select the closest Funding Area; the OFI will be triaged by staff and routed to the internal department best suited to review it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Title clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: The Project Title should clearly, concisely, and in non-technical terms convey the essence of your proposed project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use plain language; avoid dense technical jargon so the title communicates the project's essence succinctly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive Summary accessibility and content
rubrics_metrics.description: The Executive Summary should be written in such a manner that it would be comprehensible to a typical reader of the New York Times or London Times—someone who is intellectually engaged, but not necessarily a specialist in your area of expertise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A good Executive Summary will answer—in brief—all the following questions: (a) What specific questions will the project help to answer? (b) What activities will you carry out to answer those questions? (c) Why is this project needed? (d) What concrete deliverables will you produce by the end of the project? (e) What impact will your project have? Do not include project team, organization, request amount, or project duration in the Executive Summary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Description detail and specificity
rubrics_metrics.description: The Project Description is the longest and most important field in the OFI. Please provide a specific, concise, and detailed description of the activities you plan to carry out with the funds that you are requesting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If special characters, graphs, figures, or formatting are required, upload a document and type 'See attached document' in the field to refer staff to the uploaded file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of Significance
rubrics_metrics.description: The Statement of Significance should describe the current conditions in the field(s) relevant to the project, identify the problems that the project will address, and articulate the specific opportunity that your project presents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain why the problem/opportunity matters in the broader field and how your project addresses it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outputs / Deliverables
rubrics_metrics.description: The Outputs (sometimes called 'deliverables') are important events and work products that your Project activities will generate and which are necessary in order for you to make progress towards your proposed Outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a list of the outputs you intend to produce; outputs should be concrete and clearly tied to activities described in the Project Description.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcomes (5-year horizon)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Outcomes (sometimes called goals, results, or impacts) are the specific and identifiable changes that you expect your Outputs will bring about (or contribute to bringing about) within 5 years of your project’s end date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe what success would look like and list the outcomes expected as a result of your outputs; outcomes should be specific and time-bound to the 5-year post-project window.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capacity for Success (team/organization suitability)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Capacity for Success should explain why your team and/or organization is positioned to be successful in this project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include relevant experience, capabilities, infrastructure, and other factors that demonstrate your ability to deliver the proposed project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment with Sir John Templeton's Donor Intent
rubrics_metrics.description: Please explain how your proposed project would advance the philanthropic vision of Sir John Templeton and aligns with his Donor Intent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to the Foundation's Funding Areas page for further context and explicitly connect project goals to donor intent and Foundation priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of similarity to prior Templeton grants
rubrics_metrics.description: To the best of your knowledge is the work of the proposed project similar to, or does it further expand the work of, an active or closed grant you (or your organization) received from the John Templeton Foundation, the Templeton World Charity Foundation, or the Templeton Religion Trust? If yes, please explain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If yes, explain (a) how the proposed project is similar to/ builds upon or expands the prior grant, and (b) provide specific information for the prior grant: Project Title, Grant ID#, Grant Amount, end date, and a brief synopsis of activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposed Project Start Date timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Your Proposed Project Start Date should be at least 6 weeks after the end of the relevant funding cycle (i.e., the applicant notification date).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review the Foundation’s grantmaking calendar prior to submitting your OFI because the timing of review affects when projects can start.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project duration limits by recipient type
rubrics_metrics.description: The maximum permissible duration of your project will depend on the type of organization receiving the grant. For most organizations that are recognized as public charities in the United States, the Proposed Project End Date must be no more than 36 months beyond the Proposed Project Start Date. For all other organizations and grants to individuals, the Proposed Project End Date should not be more than 33 months beyond the Proposed Project Start Date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan project duration according to organization classification and ensure end date falls within the allowed maximum for your organization type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary Contact responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The Primary Contact is the person who will manage all communications with the Foundation regarding the funding request. As the originator of this OFI you are the Primary Contact (unless another person submits using their account).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To change/update the Primary Contact information, email portal support. Another person can create a Templeton Portal account to submit as Primary Contact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Leader / Principal Investigator requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The Project Leader is the person who will take the overall leadership role in the project. Provide required information on the Project Leader, including an upload of the Project Leader’s CV/resume. If the PL is an academic, provide their 16-digit ORCiD ID.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Project Leader may also be the Primary Contact. If the Project Leader differs from the Primary Contact, supply full required info. Anyone needing an ORCiD can get one at orcid.org.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Co-Leader / Co-Investigator requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The Project Co-Leader works alongside the Project Leader. If relevant, provide required information on the Project Co-Leader, including CV/resume and ORCiD if academic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Co-Leader may be the Primary Contact or there may be none; upload CV/resume as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict/related-party disclosure for leaders
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Project Leader or Co-Leader is related to the Foundation as described in Question 14 in the OFI, please email programofficer@templeton.org to seek further advice before submitting your inquiry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criteria for answering 'Yes' is if the Project Leader or Co-Leader (or their spouse or family) presently serve as a Trustee, Officer, or staff member of the Foundation. Serving on the Board of Advisors (current or past) or being related to someone who has served on that advisory board should be answered 'No'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional personnel details
rubrics_metrics.description: For each additional personnel that has already committed to your proposed project, provide their full name, disciplinary and organizational affiliation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional personnel may include co-leaders, consultants, post-docs, presenters, speakers, panelists, or other roles required by the project.

rubrics_metrics.name: How you learned about the Foundation / prior interactions
rubrics_metrics.description: Please describe how you or any members of your team came to learn about the Foundation. Have you previously applied for or received funding? Have you participated in Foundation events or discussed your project with staff?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose prior applications, awards, event participation, or staff discussions to provide context about organizational familiarity with the Foundation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organization location and applicant capacity
rubrics_metrics.description: Select the country or area where the organization seeking funding is located. If seeking funding in your individual capacity (funds will be paid to you), answer 'Yes'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide correct location/capacity information; this affects eligibility, ER applicability, and contracting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organization name and department details
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide the full name of the college or university (do not use abbreviations). Provide the specific department or center within a college or university and any alternative names or translations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If your organization’s answer to certain eligibility questions triggers restrictions, email programofficer@templeton.org for guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expenditure Responsibility (ER) overview
rubrics_metrics.description: The IRS requires private foundations to exercise 'Expenditure Responsibility' over grants to organizations which are: For Profit; Not classified as a Public Charity in the United States; or A newly formed Public Charity with a limited budget or history.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If your Organization falls into these categories and your request is approved, you will be required to operate under ER and provide Expenditure Responsibility Reports for the duration of the grant, including reporting of capital expenditures purchased with grant funds. Additional details provided if invited to Full Proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capital expenditure definition
rubrics_metrics.description: In general, capital expenditures include items with an individual value equal to or greater than $5,000 USD (or foreign currency equivalent), which have a 'useful life' of more than one year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Equipment (vehicles, office equipment, computer equipment, research/lab equipment, aggregated interdependent equipment), Website (application/infrastructure development, domain acquisition, software/database/apps, hardware installation/testing), Software (development, apps, databases front-end/back-end).

rubrics_metrics.name: What is not a capital expenditure
rubrics_metrics.description: Equipment, website, or software expenditures of less than $5,000 USD (or foreign currency equivalent) or with a useful life of less than one year are not capital.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also not capital: (1) aggregate costs of individual pieces used independently (example: 3 laptops costing $2,000 each totaling $6,000), (2) costs to lease items from a third party, (3) website costs related to planning, content development, and operating.

rubrics_metrics.name: JTF limits on ER grants and capital expenditures
rubrics_metrics.description: JTF has its own internal project duration maximum of 33 months for ER grants. This may limit ability to provide funding for capital expenditures with a useful life of greater than 3 years. Capital expenditures with a useful life exceeding 5 years, such as office furniture, may NOT be purchased with JTF grant funds. Buildings and significant building improvements may NOT be purchased with JTF grant funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If invited to submit a Full Proposal, additional ER and capital-expenditure details will be provided; plan purchases and timelines accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepted grant payment currencies
rubrics_metrics.description: The Foundation awards and pays grants in sixteen (16) different currencies: USD, AUD, CAD, CHF, DKK, EUR, GBP, HKD, ILS, JPY, MXN, NZD, SEK, SGD, TRY, and ZAR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select one of the accepted currencies in the OFI budget fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request amount formatting and indirect costs
rubrics_metrics.description: How much funding are you requesting from the Foundation? The Foundation will approve an added component for overhead/indirect costs within the budget, which is no more than (fifteen) 15% and welcomes proposals that request a lower percentage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Round to the nearest whole currency unit and use numbers only in amount fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Total Project Amount definition and preference for co-funding
rubrics_metrics.description: The Total Project Amount may be equal to or greater than the Request Amount. The Total Project Amount is the sum of: (a) the Request Amount and (b) funding secured or requested specifically for this project from other sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Foundation favors projects in which a proportion of the required funding has been secured from other sources. Round to whole units.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget Narrative purpose and content at OFI stage
rubrics_metrics.description: The purpose of the Budget Narrative at this early stage helps the Foundation determine if the estimated project expenses are reasonable and necessary for the proposed project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a broad overview in narrative or bullets of proposed expenses including anticipated amounts and major categories. Additionally, list supplementary sources of funding for your project, the amount secured/requested, and the status of each request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and examples of Additional Funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional Funding can include funds from other philanthropic organizations, in-kind support from the employers of project personnel, or donated time of project members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional Funding does NOT include costs for equipment not solely used for the proposed project (e.g., an fMRI scanner), costs for activities associated with but not specifically part of the proposed project (e.g., a larger conference that precedes a proposed workshop), nor support for activities that will occur before or after the project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review and submit finalization rules
rubrics_metrics.description: This page provides applicants with the opportunity to review the contents of your funding inquiry, download a copy of the current form, and identify any missing fields or fields that exceed the character limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If all required fields are complete and within character limits, applicants will be able to submit their OFI. Once submitted the record becomes read only and you will not be able to make any edits to your submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attachment instruction for special formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: If the description of your project requires the use of special characters, graphs, figures, or formatting, you may upload a document in the space provided and type in the phrase 'See attached document' to refer staff to your uploaded file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the upload facility for content that cannot be entered cleanly into the text field; explicitly reference attachments in the text to alert reviewers.
